metadata.case_name: FOHG PAK LAM v. CHAN TAT TRADING AS TAI YUEN AND THE OFFICIAL RECEIVER AND TRUSTEE OF CHAN TAI TRADING AS TAI YUEN, A BANKRUPT

plaintiff.occupation_after: relieving or odd-job worker; employed by elder brother doing masonry work in decorating premises

injuries.description: perforating injury to his left eye; 100% visual disability to the left eye
source: These medical reports confirmed that the Plaintiff, following a perforating injury to his left eye, had suffered a 100% visual disability to the left eye.
Dr. W.J. Heffernan, in his second report dated 17th June 1986, stated that the eye defect was permanent and constituted a 25% defect in the visual system and a 24% defect in the Whole Man.
injuries.icd_description: Penetrating wound of eyeball without foreign body, unilateral

manifestations.description: intense pain to his left eye overnight following the accident
The Plaintiff gave evidence that he cannot see at all with his left eye
Because his field of vision is restricted

treatments_received: Follow-up outpatient treatment at Yaumati Eye Clinic
Purchase of contact lens and sunglasses

losses.description: The Plaintiff gave evidence that he cannot see at all with his left eye and this causes inconvenience in his work as a stone mason or decoration worker making it difficult for him to retain a job.
He says he is only employed as a relieving or odd-job worker because of his sight defect. An employer soon becomes aware of his sight disability.
He considers his prospects of getting married have been reduced because of his eye injury and its effect on his earning capacity in the future.
